key_difference: (B) rejects every percent-encoded byte >= 0x80, because valid UTF-8 is already folded to UTF-16 before decode() runs, and on Windows it also rejects literal backslashes stored in decoded form; (D) instead re-decodes %80-%FF as UTF-8 through a new traits struct, adds a fallback that copies the input undecoded when there is a bad-encoding sequence, and has no Windows literal-'\\' check, so a decoded backslash reaches the output on Windows.
